subject: Renewal: converting Orchard to AWS Marketplace billing
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morales <dana.morales@orchard.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal: converting Orchard to AWS Marketplace billing

Hi Dana —

Congrats again on the renewal coming up next month. Orchard is a great fit for a marketplace billing conversion and co-sell play, and we’ve been able to preserve ARR while moving several customers onto the Marketplace in ways that simplify procurement and shorten PO cycles.

High level ask: would Orchard be open to a billing swap to AWS Marketplace for the renewal term? The benefits on our side: simplified invoicing for you, ability to get marketplace incentives for partner teams, and a single entitlement flow for seat/usage reporting. For Orchard: one contract via AWS, faster procurement approvals, and consolidated billing.

I attached a short migration checklist and an initial SOW that describes the amendment flow. If this works, we’ll propose an addendum to the existing MSA (we can add a marketplace addendum) and route it through DocuSign. Two quick questions to help scope:
- Does Procurement require invoices to remain on your side with a specific invoice cadence?
- Any internal constraints on marketplace SKUs (metering vs subscription)?

If helpful I can set a 30-minute handoff with procurement + our finance/legal. Suggest Feb 15 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Redwood-SOW-v2.pdf, type: application/pdf)
From: Dana Morales <dana.morales@orchard.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orchard.ai>, Thomas Li <thomas.li@orchard.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: converting Orchard to AWS Marketplace billing

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the heads up. High level sounds promising but procurement has two main concerns: 1) we have an active commitment with Redwood that includes volume discounts tied to direct invoices; will converting to marketplace impact those discounts? 2) timing: our renewal paperwork needs a firm signature by 03/01 to avoid lapses.

Can you confirm:
- Whether existing discounts/committed pricing can be preserved or mirrored in a marketplace SKU?
- If we move to marketplace, when will Redwood send the first invoice and how will refunds / credits be handled for any pro-rated items?

Looping Thomas from procurement to coordinate details.

—Dana
Head of Finance Ops, Orchard AI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dana Morales <dana.morales@orchard.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: converting Orchard to AWS Marketplace billing

Hi Dana — Ben here, Sales Engineer. Quick answers:

- We can preserve committed economics by issuing a marketplace SKUs + a vendor-managed discount profile. Practically that looks like either: a) a one-to-one SKU that matches your direct plan with an attached entitlement that replicates the committed seat tiers, or b) a metered SKU combined with a reservation (if you prefer usage flexibility). We’ll map your current committed quantities to Marketplace entitlements so the price/discount remains intact.

- Invoices: once the conversion is live, AWS invoices the subscription according to the cadence you choose. For pro-rates and credits in the conversion month, Redwood will issue a one-time credit note to reconcile any overlap — we can handle this as part of the amendment.

I attached a short migration checklist (marketplace-migration-checklist.xlsx) that outlines the sequence: vendor registration, SKU mapping, entitlement sync, DocuSign amendment, and go-live smoke tests.

Happy to run through the checklist with your procurement team on the call.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: marketplace-migration-checklist.xlsx, type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Thomas Li <thomas.li@orchard.ai>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orchard.ai>
Date: 2027-02-12T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: converting Orchard to AWS Marketplace billing

Thanks Ben — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:
- We need a written note from Redwood confirming the committed discount will be preserved for the first 12 months after migration.
- For internal audit we need a timeline for entitlement sync and a test plan for billing validation before we cutover.

If you can send those items (confirmation note + test plan) we can sign off internally.

—Thomas
Senior Procurement Manager, Orchard AI
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Li <thomas.li@orchard.ai>, Dana Morales <dana.morales@orchard.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-13T13:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: converting Orchard to AWS Marketplace billing

Hi Thomas / Dana —

Laura from Legal/Finance here. I’ve attached a redline of the marketplace amendment (Redwood-Marketplace-MPA-redline.docx). Key notes:
- Clause 3.2 (pricing preservation) has language to explicitly mirror the committed discount for the initial 12-month period post-migration.
- We propose a 30-day reconciliation window for any pro-rated offsets; Redwood will issue credits within that window.
- Audit evidence: SOC2 Type II report and historic invoice samples will be provided via the secure link after NDA is executed (we can provide a limited access package to procurement for verification).

We’re ready to route the amendment via DocuSign once you confirm the redline and the proposed call time (Vivek proposed Feb 15 10:00 AM PT).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Contracting & Finance, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Redwood-Marketplace-MPA-redline.docx, type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Great — thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Summary and next steps:

1) Redwood will preserve the committed discount for 12 months post-migration (language in redline).
2) Redwood will provide a test plan / entitlement sync schedule by EOD 2027-02-15. Ben will own the technical validation; Laura will own contractual steps and credits.
3) We’ll route the amendment via DocuSign once Orchard confirms the redline. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/rdw-orchard-amendment
4) Proposed call: Feb 15, 10:00 AM PT — 30 minute procurement + finance handoff. Please confirm availability.

Attachments for your reference: Redwood-SOW-v2.pdf; marketplace-migration-checklist.xlsx; Redwood-Marketplace-MPA-redline.docx

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/278944/4782

Thanks — looking forward to closing the renewal and moving Orchard onto marketplace billing.
